_note: Digging on the street map (ui/innerMapDigging.js): holes, filling them in, graves. Seconds are real seconds of work at the spot; carrying a set of tools (any item id in 'tools') multiplies them by toolSpeed. 'finds' are rolled once per hole, in order: the first whose chance hits is found.

finds.text: Your spade turns up {gold} gold coins, buried long ago.
You turn up a broken clay pot. Nothing of worth.
An old bone, brown with age. Best not to wonder whose.

text.dig: You dig a hole, the spoil heaped beside it.
text.fill: You shovel the earth back in and tread it down.
text.bury: You lay {name} in the hole and heap the earth over them.
text.exhume: You dig down to {name}: the grave lies open, the earth heaped beside it.
respects: You stand a while by {name}'s grave.
You bow your head over {name}'s grave.
You say a word for {name}, {years} in the ground.
respectsMound: You stand a while by the bare mound where {name} lies.
You bow your head over the turned earth. Only you know it is {name} under it.
text.cache: You bury {what} and fill the hole in over it.
text.cacheGone: The earth here has been dug over before you. Whatever was buried here is gone.
text.cacheGoneSeen: You remember {name} watching you bury it.

_burial: A body buried by the player (world/burials.js; ui/innerMapDigging.js) is a plain, unmarked mound: named 'Burial Mound', not the grave of anyone. freshDays: days a mound is bare, dark, freshly turned earth (no grass, no flowers) before it weathers into the churchyard's grassed mound; settleDays: days for an unmarked mound to settle level and the ground to grow back over it (drawn fading down to minAlpha; the record stays: still dug up, still marked). markers: what may be raised over it, the churchyards' kinds (data/graves.json markers, their art): item, a marker carried in the pack (bought at a market: grave carvers and masons make them, data/markets.json), used up when raised; carve, the wood or planks carried that a cross is carved from on the spot (the first the player has); seconds / carveSeconds the work at the spot. Dug up, a marker comes back to the pack as its item. Burials are saved on world.burials[hex]['q,r'].

text.marked: You raise a {marker} over {name}. It is a grave now, with a name on it.
text.carved: You carve a rough {marker}, cut {name}'s name into it and set it at the head of the mound.
text.alreadyMarked: A marker already stands over this grave.

_ground: How dug ground goes on the street map (world/innerMap/graves.js _settleDug, on entering a map): a hole left open (with nothing put in it) caves in to turned earth after holeCaveDays; turned earth fades back into the ground over filledFadeDays (drawn fading). A grave dug open and filled in again shows its disturbed earth for burial.disturbedDays; in a town the sexton fills in a grave left open after burial.refillDays.
_cache: Things buried in a hole (world/burials.js caches, saved on world.caches): whoever watched them go in (up to maxSeen) may come back after witnessDays at witnessChance a day; someone digging by chance turns one up at strayTown (a town map) or strayWild a day. Hash of the day, not the shared RNG.
_graveRobbers: NPC grave robbers (systems/scavengers.js; on the street map ui/innerMapScavengers.js). perNight[type]: the chance a night that someone in town robs a grave worth it (x lairMult with an outlaw lair within lairRadius hexes; lairShare of them are its men). Robbers are townsfolk of poorRoles who are beggars or crookedTraits (never honestTraits), outlaws, or in snatcherTypes towns a body-snatcher (snatcherShare) after a grave under snatcherFreshDays. weights: goods per grave good, playerGoods a burial of the player with goods, seenCache a cache someone watched buried. watchChance[type]: caught off the map. nightFrom/nightTo: the hours; digSeconds: the work on the map. Goods the town market keeps go into its stock; others are sold to a fence at fenceShare of their worth, his coin out of the town purse into a townsperson robber's purse (an outlaw or snatcher carries them off).

graveRobbers._digSeconds: digSeconds: a robber's work at a grave bare-handed; with a spade × toolSpeed (the player's own rule above), a cache's shallow hole × seconds.dig / seconds.exhume. Body-snatchers and outlaws come with a spade, a townsperson toolShare of the time.

_looters: NPC looters (systems/scavengers.js; ui/innerMapScavengers.js): every scanSeconds, someone within radius of a fallen person (dead, senseless, bound; the player knocked out) may go to them, kneel kneelSeconds and go through their things: chance[kind] by who they are (opportunist: opportunistTypes, beggars, crookedTraits; soldier; kin: the fallen's kin and friends, safekeeping, no theft). Coin and valuables first, then up to maxItems kinds of gear; the player loses playerGoldShare of the purse. Seen, it is the looter's crime (the watch takes them).
